findings.title: Make the target carry the blow
findings.locator: Official reader image segment 52 (one-based; not a printed page number)
findings.already_working: Our planted lunge and lifted opponent already make force visible. Faces and weapons remain readable.
findings.remaining_gap: The target is still mostly an intact, posed silhouette. The Boxer excerpt spends nearly everything on compressed flesh, a turned head and one contact.
findings.encounter_test: In one peak beat, let a shoulder collapse, a cheek compress or the grip fail. In the next, show the resulting loss of guard. Keep that consequence across the following action.
findings.comparison_limit: Different contact types: saber deflection versus a boxing punch. This is a bodily-consequence comparison, not a claim they should look identical.

findings.title: Make the escape answer a committed attack
findings.locator: Official reader image segment 51 (one-based; not a printed page number)
findings.already_working: The deep shaft, outstretched hand and wall departure create a readable route and exciting height.
findings.remaining_gap: The polished airborne silhouette can read as a travel pose. The reference makes an incoming arm and narrow evasion share one directional field.
findings.encounter_test: Show the spear committing into the old position; cut closer to the near miss, then land somewhere that changes the next tactical choice.
findings.comparison_limit: The reference is an overhead boxing evasion, not the same power or setting. Borrow the spatial relationship, not anatomy or clothing.

findings.title: A close frame needs a dangerous gap
findings.locator: Official reader image segment 43 (one-based; not a printed page number)
findings.already_working: Our ink wedges, clenched expression and enlarged contact make a stronger peak than a distant neutral exchange.
findings.remaining_gap: The opposing torso and weapon can still feel staged around a flash. The reference brings a blade immediately beside a tilted face.
findings.encounter_test: Use one tight reaction or guard-failure frame inside the encounter. Preserve the blade path and frightened or defiant eye without surrounding it with more microtexture.
findings.comparison_limit: The reference has glitter and prismatic edges we should not automatically adopt. Its tight crop does not establish all grips.

findings.title: A power can become the environment
findings.locator: Official reader image segment 23 (one-based; not a printed page number)
findings.already_working: The broad pale diagonal plane, displaced enemies and anchored caster give our ability a clear, unusual identity.
findings.remaining_gap: A reveal can look impressive before we understand its price or tactical use. The huge black sweep is also a scale reveal, not a complete action chain.
findings.encounter_test: Let the power remove a specific option: turn safe ground into a fall, interrupt a charge, or divide allies. Show the limitation before its next use.
findings.comparison_limit: Both examples omit parts of the causal sequence in a single frame. Large area or bright contrast alone is not proof of combat readability.

findings.title: Keep horror quiet; make proximity costly
findings.reference_title: Solo Leveling — Volume 3 — publisher Look inside preview
findings.locator: Look inside preview image 015 (preview index, not printed page number)
findings.already_working: Our restrained grayscale, pale face and oversized masked creature already create a distinct horror language.
findings.remaining_gap: The low fencing pose and looming creature remain controlled. The reference’s mouth and tight face crop eliminate safe distance.
findings.encounter_test: Keep the quiet surfaces. Show a failed escape, a weapon pinned against a claw, or a face reacting to a tiny remaining gap; then make the survivor change strategy.
findings.comparison_limit: The reference is colorful monster action, not a horror-style target. Its useful feature is proximity and reaction, not palette or creature design.

findings.title: Weight needs an understandable pivot
findings.reference_title: The God of High School — Episode 6
findings.locator: Official reader image segment 14 (one-based; not a printed page number)
findings.already_working: The warm painting, loaded legs and heavy construct give this direction a strong material and combat identity.
findings.remaining_gap: A huge creature can appear conveniently airborne if the load transfer is not explicit. The simple throw reference exposes a planted pivot and a displaced body center.
findings.encounter_test: Before the heavy counter, show the construct committing weight onto a support. Let a visible leverage point or failed support explain the fall; retain the changed footing afterward.
findings.comparison_limit: Human throwing is not a literal mechanism for moving a giant machine. The transferable idea is an evident pivot and a cost-bearing stance.

findings.title: Let personality survive the impact
findings.reference_title: The God of High School — Episode 6
findings.locator: Official reader image segment 18 (one-based; not a printed page number)
findings.already_working: Our broad color shapes, laughing expression and large hammer produce an appealing, playful kind of power.
findings.remaining_gap: A smiling hero and floating armored target can read as a celebratory poster. The reference isolates the victim’s long ballistic trajectory.
findings.encounter_test: Give the launch an awkward bodily follow-through or tumbling landing. Keep the hero’s exuberance while allowing the opponent to interrupt it in the next beat.
findings.comparison_limit: Comic exuberance and gritty violence are independent choices. This reference shows consequence after a blow, not the contact itself.

findings.title: A skill needs rules beyond its color
findings.locator: Official reader image segment 37 (one-based; not a printed page number)
findings.already_working: Our source-to-spear fire bend, separate caster and displaced defenders create a relatively understandable power interaction.
findings.remaining_gap: A beautiful arc can become a repeated decorative solution. The reference shows how large simple forms can establish a distinct power family.
findings.encounter_test: Define what the redirect can and cannot bend, where the force exits and what exposes the user. Let the next enemy exploit that rule before an earned adaptation.
findings.comparison_limit: The reference is a magic reveal with luminous spheres, not a fire-deflection action. Borrow consistent visual grammar, not those forms or colors.
